query: For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to the untreated reference, applicable boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: The application of a chromium-rich coating with a thickness of 1-25 μm to Q235 steel will reduce the corrosion rate and increase corrosion resistance compared to the untreated reference, with optimal performance at a coating thickness of 10-15 μm, due to the cathodic protection and barrier effect of the chromium-rich coating.
generation.material_initial_state: Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state
generation.intervention: Application of a chromium-rich coating with varying thicknesses (1-25 μm) using electroplating
generation.conditions: Exposure to 3.5% NaCl solution at room temperature (20°C) and elevated temperature (60°C)
generation.mechanism: Cathodic protection and barrier effect of the chromium-rich coating
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced corrosion rate and increased corrosion resistance compared to the untreated reference, with optimal performance at a coating thickness of 10-15 μm
generation.boundary: Coating thickness range of 1-25 μm, exposure to 3.5% NaCl solution at room and elevated temperatures
generation.uncertainty: The optimal coating thickness may not be within the proposed range, and the effectiveness of the chromium-rich coating may vary in different harsh environments

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled study with multiple replicates, using electroplating to apply the chromium-rich coating with varying thicknesses (1-25 μm) to Q235 steel, and exposing the samples to 3.5% NaCl solution at room temperature (20°C) and elevated temperature (60°C)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate is not reduced and corrosion resistance is not increased compared to the untreated reference, the hypothesis is falsified
